mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of co-contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 1 percentage point within a month, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL of more than 0.4% month-over-month, signals aggressive tightening and rising inflation, which together depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > +1% in a month AND CPIAUCSL change > +0.4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in PAYEMS of more than 0.3% for four consecutive months signals weakening employment and income growth, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -0.3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS for three consecutive months signals a reduction in consumer savings, which may presage increased consumption and higher inflation, but also fiscal tightening, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days under expansionary monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < 0 for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered expansionary episodes.
